the color-magnitude relations of early-type galaxies in local clusters can be reproduced in a self-consistent manner by means of a chemical evolution model, with outflows as the main mechanism for chemical enrichment.

the color-magnitude and mass-to-light relations of early-type galaxies in local clusters can be explained in terms of outflows and infall, without invoking a strong dependence on the star formation efficiency and the star formation history.

chemical enrichment tracks can provide a simple and useful way to constrain the evolution of early-type galaxies.
